Interface FeatureFlag<T>

Type Parameters:
T - the flag value type
public interface FeatureFlag<T>
A feature flag.

Feature flags are defined via FeatureFlagService.define(String, boolean) and are bound to the service's cache and lifecycle.

Since:
0.24.0

    • getExpiration

      @Contract(pure=true) Optional<Instant> getExpiration()
      Get the expiration time for the current cached value.

      If no value has been cached yet, this returns Optional.empty(). The returned timestamp indicates when the cached value should be treated as stale according to the configured TTL.

      Returns:
      the expiration time of the cached value, if present
      Since:
      0.24.0
      See Also:
      • isValid()

    • isExpired

      @Contract(pure=true) boolean isExpired()
      Returns whether the current cached value is expired.

      A value is expired when no fetch has completed yet or when the configured TTL has elapsed since the last fetch.

      Returns:
      true if the cached value is absent or stale
      Since:
      0.24.0
      See Also:
      • getExpiration()
      • isValid()

    • isValid

      @Contract(pure=true) boolean isValid()
      Returns whether the current cached value is still valid.

      A value is valid when it is cached and its configured TTL has not yet expired. This method is non-blocking and never performs a network request.

      Returns:
      true if a non-expired cached value is available
      Since:
      0.24.0

    • whenReady

      CompletableFuture<T> whenReady()
      Return a future that completes with the flag value once it is ready.

      If the value is valid according to isValid(), the returned future completes immediately. Otherwise, a new fetch is performed and the future completes when the response arrives.

      Returns:
      a future completing with the flag value
      Since:
      0.24.0
      See Also:
      • fetch()

    • fetch

      @Contract(mutates="this") CompletableFuture<T> fetch()
      Force a fresh fetch of the flag value from the server.

      Unlike whenReady(), this always performs a server request.

      The returned future may complete exceptionally if the request fails, the server returns a non-successful response, or the response body cannot be parsed as the requested flag type. The most common non-successful response is an unknown flag identifier.

      Failed fetches do not update the cached value. Failure details are only logged when debug logging is enabled.

      While submission is not active, for example before the user gave consent or on the first run of a server, no request is sent and the future completes with the default value. The cached value is not updated.

      Returns:
      a future completing with the latest server value
      Since:
      0.24.0
      See Also:
      • whenReady()

    • optIn

      @Contract(mutates="this") CompletableFuture<T> optIn()
      Request that the server opt in to this flag, then invalidate the local value and fetch the current server value again.

      This sends a POST /v1/flag/opt-in request. The server determines the resulting flag value based on its own conditions.

      The returned future completes with the updated value after the local cache has been reset and the follow-up fetch finishes. It completes exceptionally with an IllegalStateException if submission is not active.

      Returns:
      a future completing with the updated flag value
      Since:
      0.24.0
      See Also:
      • fetch()
